title: OpenEAGO Financial-Services Domain Vocabulary
$comment: Canonical controlled vocabulary for regulated financial-services agentic workflows. All string-typed fields in OpenEAGO schemas that reference compliance frameworks, capability types, or regulatory profiles MUST use values defined here. This is the single source of truth for shared semantics — it is what makes two independent implementations interoperable at the meaning layer, not just the wire layer.

compliance_profile.title: Compliance Profile
compliance_profile.description: A regulatory framework or standard that applies to a workflow or agent interaction. Values are the canonical short-form identifiers used by the specification.

capability_type.title: Regulated Capability Type
capability_type.description: A named, regulated operation that an agent can perform. These identifiers establish the shared ontology: two agents agree that 'kyc_verification' means the same thing because the spec defines it, not because they happened to use the same string. Extension capabilities outside this vocabulary MUST use the prefix 'x-' (e.g. 'x-trade_surveillance'). When 'audit_anchoring' or 'identity_verification' fires for a given decision, record it via that decision record's own 'attestation' object (see validation-compliance.schema.json and execution-resilience.schema.json), not via this enum.

regulatory_profile.title: Regulatory Profile
regulatory_profile.description: The primary jurisdictional and regulatory context in which a workflow executes. Used during planning to scope data-residency, cross-border clearance, and compliance framework selection.

policy_check.title: Well-Known Policy Check
policy_check.description: Canonical identifiers for policy checks that implementations MAY record in the policy_checks array. The policy_checks field is not enum-constrained — organisations may use custom checks. These well-known values ensure that checks with cross-implementation significance use consistent identifiers.

description: This schema is a vocabulary reference document, not a payload schema. It does not validate message payloads directly. Individual phase schemas import vocabulary values from the $defs above. See SPECIFICATION.md §3B for the domain vocabulary normative requirements.
